smeFieldKnowledge.topic: Georgia Red Clay Soil Foundation Settlement
smeFieldKnowledge.smeInsight: Georgia red clay is highly expansive. During rainy seasons, it swells against foundation walls; during summer droughts, it contracts and leaves voids. This creates stair-step mortar cracks in brick facades and causes crawlspace brick piers to tilt.
smeFieldKnowledge.actionableAdvice: Ensure gutters discharge at least 6 feet away from foundation walls and maintain positive landscaping slope.

smeFieldKnowledge.smeInsight: Common in 1980s-1990s Metro Atlanta subdivisions (Alpharetta, Sandy Springs, Duluth). Chlorine in municipal water degrades gray polybutylene pipes internally without surface signs until sudden wall blowout.
smeFieldKnowledge.actionableAdvice: Use FLIR thermal cameras to check behind vanities and main shutoffs for micro-leaks before full re-pipe failure.

smeFieldKnowledge.topic: Federal Pacific & Zinsco Electrical Panel Fire Hazards
smeFieldKnowledge.smeInsight: Widespread in mid-century Metro Atlanta homes (Decatur, East Lake, Smyrna). Stab-Lok breakers fail to trip on electrical overload, creating severe arc flash fire hazards.
smeFieldKnowledge.actionableAdvice: Recommend 100% seller credit or immediate licensed electrician panel replacement prior to closing.

smeFieldKnowledge.smeInsight: High humidity in North Georgia causes 80%+ wood moisture saturation in crawlspaces. Floor joists absorb water, causing hardwood flooring to cup and subfloors to rot.
smeFieldKnowledge.actionableAdvice: Install 6-mil minimum vapor barrier covering 100% of exposed crawlspace soil and consider encapsulation.
